candidates.lead: Women with endometriosis are suffering financially as well as physically, a new report by MPs warns
candidates.evidence_text: 'Some think endometriosis is just a bad period, but it's so much worse' - BBC News Image source, Chloe Ward Image caption, Chloe Ward says years of treatment, surgery and time off work have left her paying a heavy financial price for endometriosis By James Fell and Mat Trewern , North West Published 1 hour ago Women with endometriosis are being forced out of work, losing income and facing significant financial hardship because of the condition, according to a new report by MPs. The inquiry by the All-Party Parliamentary Group on Endometriosis, supported by Endometriosis UK, found 47% of women with the condition had lost income because of their symptoms, while 28% had left a job altogether. Among them was Chloe Ward, from Bolton, who said her endometriosis - which can cause severe pain, fatigue, heavy bleeding and fertility problems - had cost her thousands of pounds and affected her ability to run her own business. She said: "A lot of people think it's just a bad period, but it's so much worse." About one in 10 women suffer from the condition, but diagnosis can be a lengthy process. Chloe said it took seven years for her to be diagnosed. She said being self-employed in the beauty industry meant she had flexibility, but no financial safety net. "If I'm not there to do the treatments, nobody pays me," she said. She told BBC Radio Manchester she had lost clients over the years because flare-ups could leave her unable to work at short notice. Image source, Chloe Ward Image caption, Endo the Night encourages people to host fundraising events while raising awareness of endometriosis Chloe is now waiting for a hysterectomy, which will mean more time away from work. "There's so much to it that people don't understand," she said. The financial impact has extended beyond lost earnings. After receiving a stage-four endometriosis diagnosis in 2023, she paid about £6,000 for private surgery because NHS waiting times were too long. She and her partner also spent about £8,000 on a third round of IVF after two NHS-funded attempts failed. The report found 39% of women with endometriosis had experienced financial hardship because of the condition, while 40% said they had turned down career opportunities due to a lack of workplace support. Image source, Megan Gomersall Image caption, Megan Gomersall has been out of work for about two and a half years because of her symptoms Megan Gomersall, 30, from Rochdale, said the condition ended a career she loved. The former paediatric nurse has been out of work for about two and a half years because of her symptoms. She said endometriosis, which affects her bladder and bowel, left her in severe pain during shifts and frequently off sick before she received a diagnosis. It took 13 years for her condition to be identified. "It has been really, really difficult," she said. "It's been like a grieving process in a way. I feel like I've completely lost my identity and purpose." Megan said she believed more could be done to help women remain in work through reasonable adjustments and greater awareness of the condition. The inquiry found fewer than half of employees with endometriosis had received workplace adjustments, while 94% believed employers lacked a good understanding of the condition. A Department of Health and Social Care spokesperson said endometriosis can have a "devastating impact" on women's lives and said the government's renewed Women's Health Strategy identifies it as a priority condition. The spokesperson said the findings highlighted the need for better support, both in healthcare and in the workplace. You can also send story ideas via Whatsapp to 0808 100 2230. candidates.evidence_text: The Wanted: Late Tom Parker 'always there', says bandmate - BBC News Image caption, The Wanted's Max George said hearing late bandmate Tom Parker's voice is his favourite part of being of stage By Anna Jameson and Georgie Docker , North West Published 1 hour ago With four million singles and a million album sales under their belts, The Wanted were one of the biggest boy bands in the 2010s. After breaking through onto the music scene in America, the band enjoyed global success before tragedy struck when Bolton-born Tom Parker died from a brain tumour in 2022 at the age of 33. As band members Max George and Siva Kaneswaran set off on tour as The Wanted 2.0, George, from Swinton, in Manchester, spoke to BBC North West Tonight about Parker, returning to the stage as a two-piece, and going through heart surgery. He spoke ahead of The Wanted 2.0 performing at Manchester Academy on Friday. The Wanted formed as a five-piece boy band in 2009, and had Max George, Siva Kaneswaran, Jay McGuiness, Tom Parker, and Nathan Sykes in the line-up. "It was a shock because I'd never, ever thought that I'd ever be in a band that was successful," George said. Image source, PA Image caption, Max George and Siva Kaneswaran performing together as The Wanted 2.0 The bandmembers had each been selected as part of a mass open audition held by talent manager Jayne Collins, who had also put together The Saturdays. "I was sort of in so I could afford just to have a few beers at the weekend, go out with my mates and put a roof over my head," George said. "That was my vision with it because I loved doing it." Image caption, The Wanted's first single All Time Low was released in 2010, putting them into the UK charts But in May 2011 the band released Glad You Came. It was the second single from their second album was released, and it changed everything. "All of a sudden it took off," George recalled. "Our record label rang me and said it was selling over 300,000 copies a week. "I was just mind-blown." He said the success in America brought the band a whole new level of fame. "It was life-changing," he said. "Obviously we'd had success here. "But when you get it on a scale somewhere as big as America, it really does change your life. "The number of people that come to see you and recognise you walking through New York... was just crazy." Image source, PA Image caption, Tom Parker was diagnosed with an incurable brain tumour in 2020 The band announced they were having a break in January 2014. Six years later, Parker was diagnosed with inoperable stage four glioblastoma. The Wanted released their first single in seven years in October 2021, followed by a greatest hits album the next month. After accompanying the band on a 12-date UK tour, Parker died in March 2022. "I think with any loss you have days that are terrible, but then weeks where you feel fine. And then all of a sudden you think 'Why have I not been upset the last few weeks? "I think that's just the way that you deal with stuff." George is currently embarking on tour with Kaneswaran. It is the second tour the pair have done since Parker's death. "I get reminded [of Tom] all the time," George said. "Me and Tom always used to be in each other's ears because we'd sing together on lead vocals. "I still have his voice playing in my ears when we're on stage. "He's always there which is lovely for me. I love that. "It's my favourite thing about doing the show." Image source, PA Image caption, The Wanted 2.0 are currently touring the UK on their (We're) Glad You Came tour Since The Wanted 2.0's first toured in America in 2024, George has been through a health scare of his own. Nearly two years ago, doctors discovered he had a blockage in his heart, requiring urgent surgery. "I had the pacemaker put in but then it became apparent that there was a mistake," he said. "That made me even worse. "So I had to have it removed and put back in and it took me about a year to get over it." He said he had to get through his illness, not just for himself, but for his family. "When you're so ill you're not really that scared yourself," George said. "You just feel out of it." "But when you see that look in your mum's eyes and you see what it's doing to her.. that's the bit that wakes you up and makes you think 'God, I have to get through this'. George added: "This is a whole new chapter with Siva. I love working, I love being on stage and forgetting about this stuff." The Wanted 2.0 kicked off their 2026 UK tour in Bat

candidates.evidence_text: Man extradited and charged with John Soyoye's murder in Moston - BBC News Image source, Police handout Image caption, John Soyoye died after being attacked in Moston, Manchester, in November 2020 Published 14 October 2026 A man has been extradited back to the UK and charged with murder in the investigation into the death of a 16-year-old in Manchester. Alexander John Soyoye, known as John, died after being stabbed in the Moston area of Manchester in November 2020. Nico de Carvalho Wilson, 24, has also been charged with manslaughter and violent disorder. Wilson, who was detained in Portugal in March and was extradited on Tuesday, appeared at Manchester Magistrates' Court earlier, Greater Manchester Police said. candidates.evidence_text: Possible gang threat to family not reviewed, Walkden fire inquest hears - BBC News Image source, Family handout Image caption, Demi, Brandon, Lacie and Lia Pearson died in the 2017 arson attack, while their mother Michelle died 20 months later By Phil McCann , Reporting from at Bolton Coroners' Court and Haider Saleem , Reporting from North West Published 14 October 2026 A police safeguarding team did not review new intelligence about possible gang threats to a family before a fatal arson attack because it did not work weekends at the time, an inquest has heard. Four children died after their home in Walkden, Salford, was firebombed on 11 December 2017. Their mother, Michelle Pearson, died of her injuries 20 months later, aged 37. Det Sgt Alison Barber said information received by Greater Manchester Police (GMP) on the Friday before the attack would not have been seen until the Monday, after the fire. Barber told Bolton Coroners' Court police safeguards were in place and "nothing much would have changed" if the reports had been reviewed. The court heard Michelle's son Kyle feared he was being targeted by a Salford gang called the A-Team. Barber, a senior officer in a police team responsible for protecting relatives of people whose lives were thought to be threatened by organised crime groups, said she had known about Kyle's concerns before the fire. Image caption, Flowers and candles were left on Jackson Street in Walkden following the deaths of the four children She said the possible gang connection had caused "significant concern" because of the gang's involvement in "disputes [and] threats to life", but she could find no evidence to corroborate his fears. The inquest heard intelligence received by GMP on Friday 8 December suggested Kyle's concerns stemmed from an incident in which his brother had attacked members of the A-Team with weapons. On the same day, police also received claims Kyle was being "sought by the A-Team due to owing money for drugs" and that his sister Demi had been "chased by female members of the gang". The court heard police had also received information suggesting members of the gang had been asked to drive past the Pearson home as part of a dispute between Kyle and Zak Bolland. Image caption, Fire crews attended the scene on Jackson Street following the arson attack in December 2017 Four men in a Renault Clio later drove past the house, the court was told. Barber said she had not been aware of that information until after the fire and did not believe it was credible that the gang had been "commissioned" to drive past the property. She said Bolland was not known to be a member of the A-Team. Barber said her team did not work weekends at the time, meaning intelligence received on the Friday would not have been reviewed until the following Monday. That, she said, "unfortunately would have been after the fire". She told the court the family already had some protection, including a marker on police systems prioritising their home for urgent responses. Image caption, Investigators examined the badly damaged family home following the fatal arson attack This was linked to separate concerns that Bolland might have been connected to a police investigation into shootings in Little Hulton, rather than the reports involving the A-Team, she said. Barber said even with the additional gang intelligence, the risk to the family's lives would have been assessed as "low". At an earlier hearing, the inquest was told police visited the Pearson home in the early hours of 11 December after Michelle called 999 to report Bolland and three other people outside . PC Gemma Quinn said she believed threats made by Bolland were "empty threats" and did not think it necessary to arrest him immediately . She told the court she had planned to arrest him two days later. PC Mike Grundy earlier told the inquest "nothing" had been done to keep the family safe in the hours before the attack. Demi Pearson, 15, her brother Brandon, eight, and sisters Lacie, seven, and Lia, three, died in the fire. Bolland and David Worrall were jailed for life in 2018 for murdering the children and were subsequently convicted of Michelle's murder in 2021. Bolland received a minimum prison term of 40 years and Worrall a minimum of 37 years. The inquest, which began on 5 October, is examining Michelle's contact with police and social services in the weeks leading up to the fire. It is scheduled to last eight weeks. candidates.evidence_text: HMOs 'targeted' as 25 incidents of vandalism in Salford linked - BBC News Image caption, Police say HMOs and houses mistaken as HMOs are being vandalised across Salford By James Fell North West Published 14 October 2026 Police are investigating 25 linked incidents of criminal damage across Salford and believe houses in multiple occupation (HMOs) are being targeted. The incidents, including smashed windows, vandalism and graffiti, have been reported since 5 October and each incident follows a similar pattern of offending, Greater Manchester Police (GMP) said. The force said the attacks on homes were in different parts of the city but they were currently being treated as linked. The most recent incident was reported on Tuesday evening. Ch Insp Lee Gridley said inquiries so far had led officers to believe "HMOs, and properties that have been mistaken for HMOs, are being targeted". "No one should be made to feel unsafe in their own home and it's not something that will be tolerated in Salford, or anywhere in Greater Manchester," he said. Officers will be carrying out patrols across Salford throughout the week while investigations continue. Detectives are trawling through CCTV and monitoring social media coverage of the incidents. A 13-year-old boy who was arrested as part of an investigation on 8 October has been released on police bail. GMP is urging anyone with information or footage to come forward. candidates.evidence_text: A bus driver was on "autopilot" before crashing into a railway bridge and injuring 15 people, a court heard, as he was given a suspended prison sentence Three people were seriously injured when the double-decker bus struck a low bridge on Barton Lane in Eccles in July 2025, tearing off its roof One victim suffered a fractured skull and several others were hurt after being ejected from the top deck Christopher Henry was sentenced to two years and eight months, suspended for two-and-a-half years, after admitting causing serious injury by dangerous driving Manchester Crown Court heard Henry ignored several low bridge warnings after taking a wrong turn while driving the 100 service between the Trafford Centre and Manchester city centre The court heard the experienced driver appeared to be driving on "autopilot" after earlier operating the single-decker 52 service, which uses Barton Lane, and may have believed he was still on that route

candidates.lead: Patsy McKie dedicated her life to bringing about change after gang violence spiralled in Manchester
candidates.evidence_text: Mural remembers anti-crime campaigner who lost son to gun crime - BBC News Image caption, Patsy McKie began campaigning against violent crime after her son's death By Kelly Foran and Lauren Hirst , North West Published 14 October 2026 A mural has been created to honour the legacy of an anti-crime campaigner who was inspired to act after her son's death. Patsy McKie's youngest son Dorrie, 20, was shot dead in the Hulme area of Manchester in 1999. Just days later, she co-founded Mothers Against Violence (MAVUK) and dedicated the rest of her life to travelling across the world to raise awareness of her anti-crime campaign. A colourful mural, created by artist Marcus Lane, has been painted at the MAVUK Hulme Centre following her death in January 2025 at the age of 77. Image caption, Patsy McKie set up Mothers Against Violence days after her son was shot dead in 1999 "She was a very bright person, even through some of the most difficult periods of her life," said her son, Ian Swanston. "She wanted to bring a sense of colour to the world. "A creative artwork representing Patsy would have to be colourful, because that's definitely what she wants." Dorrie has been about to start a sports and leisure course at college when he was shot dead amid spiralling gang violence in Manchester. Patsy believed deeply in the strength of community and in the possibility of healing, even during the most difficult of times. "She always said that if young people are doing something positive, they won't have time to do the things that are negative in our community," said Ian. "So she really wanted to be able to create spaces that allowed young people to excel." Image caption, Ian Swanston said Patsy "wanted to bring a sense of colour to the world" MAVUK was set up to support families to fight injustice, achieve their full potential and participate actively in their communities. "I think she always wanted Hulme to be a big part of her life story," said Ian. "I think she really treasured the place that she lived." Makisa Gilkes, from Jet Black Dance Academy, is just one of the people to have benefited from Patsy's work. "Born and raised in this community - and obviously in a quite deprived area - so having an area where I can develop as a person and teach other people doing dance and also to be able to do it myself and having somewhere comfortable for me to attend," she said, "it has helped us a lot". evidence_packet.summary: Patsy McKie dedicated her life to bringing about change after gang violence spiralled in Manchester
evidence_packet.evidence_text: A mural has been created to honour the legacy of an anti-crime campaigner who was inspired to act after her son's death Patsy McKie's youngest son Dorrie, 20, was shot dead in the Hulme area of Manchester in 1999 Just days later, she co-founded Mothers Against Violence (MAVUK) and dedicated the rest of her life to travelling across the world to raise awareness of her anti-crime campaign A colourful mural, created by artist Marcus Lane, has been painted at the MAVUK Hulme Centre following her death in January 2025 at the age of 77 "She was a very bright person, even through some of the most difficult periods of her life," said her son, Ian Swanston "She wanted to bring a sense of colour to the world

candidates.evidence_text: Andy Burnham had two hospitality dinners with Manchester City football club's chairman while mayor of Greater Manchester, it has emerged The PM dined with Khaldoon Al Mubarak at matches in 2017 and 2018 - but this was not detailed in a statement on Monday by the Greater Manchester Combined Authority (GMCA) about his meetings with the club Burnham has been under pressure to clarify his previous discussions with Man City since the club was found guilty of having "systematically" broken Premier League rules, which it will appeal The PM, who was mayor until June, sparked widespread controversy when he said last month he would be "really concerned" if the club's owners now sold up Separately, it has emerged that a representative from the club joined a trade mission to India this week alongside Burnham's successor as mayor of Greater Manchester Bev Craig The trade mission was organised by the business department, but as first reported in the Guardian, , external Manchester City's invitation came from the Great North, a coalition of Northern mayors and regional leaders

candidates.evidence_text: A police safeguarding team did not review new intelligence about possible gang threats to a family before a fatal arson attack because it did not work weekends at the time, an inquest has heard Four children died after their home in Walkden, Salford, was firebombed on 11 December 2017. Their mother, Michelle Pearson, died of her injuries 20 months later, aged 37 Det Sgt Alison Barber said information received by Greater Manchester Police (GMP) on the Friday before the attack would not have been seen until the Monday, after the fire Barber told Bolton Coroners' Court police safeguards were in place and "nothing much would have changed" if the reports had been reviewed The court heard Michelle's son Kyle feared he was being targeted by a Salford gang called the A-Team Barber, a senior officer in a police team responsible for protecting relatives of people whose lives were thought to be threatened by organised crime groups, said she had known about Kyle's concerns before the fire

Patsy McKie's youngest son Dorrie, 20, was shot dead in the Hulme area of Manchester in 1999 Just days later, she co-founded Mothers Against Violence (MAVUK) and dedicated the rest of her life to travelling across the world to raise awareness of her anti-crime campaign A colourful mural, created by artist Marcus Lane, has been painted at the MAVUK Hulme Centre following her death in January 2025 at the age of 77 "She was a very bright person, even through some of the most difficult periods of her life," said her son, Ian Swanston "She wanted to bring a sense of colour to the world "A creative artwork representing Patsy would have to be colourful, because that's definitely what she wants."

A medical professional and originally from Birmingham, he travelled to work an study in the city After a fortnight in the region, he decided to book himself a short stay at the deluxe high-rise on Mason Street. He told the MEN his 12-day stay cost £1,634 when he booked it online. But after just one evening, he claims to have woke up with bug bites all over his body The property is understood to have offered the individual a refund since the incident. He said: "After the first day, I got a few rashes on my body so I went to the housekeeping and they came and changed my bedding "The second night it was more obvious, I thought there was something that doesn't look right. I called the housekeeping again and they did the same thing. But I wasn't convinced, I thought there was something more than that. So, I removed the mattress and it was full of bedbugs."

candidates.evidence_text: Greater Manchester Police Warning issued as fraudsters impersonating police officers in 'incredibly sophisticated' crime Police have issued a warning following the rise of the 'incredibly sophisticated' scams Add to preferred sources Comments News Cha Police are urging people to remain vigilant as scammers impersonating police officers are targeting 'vulnerable communities' across Greater Manchester. The fraudsters are trying to convince victims to hand over personal and sensitive information The 'incredibly sophisticated type of crime' sees the scammers pretend to be police officers and ask victims about their cryptocurrency accounts A common method used by the fraudsters is to claim to be a suspect that has been arrested and found in possession of the victim's personal documents, such as their passport, driving licence or banking details. These calls can 'appear convincing' and are being made through fake GM The scammers have also asked victims about their cryptocurrency accounts on several occasions, specifically looking for their IDs, recovery phrases, and security codes. Officers would never ask anyone to share this information or move your accounts, GMP added DS Reed from our Cyber Crime Team said: "These calls are an incredibly sophisticated type of crime, and those responsible are targeting our vulnerable communities

candidates.evidence_text: Walkden Salford's A-Team gang 'drove by' Walkden house weeks before tragic fire-bombing, inquest hears Michelle Pearson and four of her children - Demi, Brandon, Lacie, and Lia - were killed in the attack in December 2017 View 7 Images (Image: MEN Med Add to preferred sources News Bethan Finighan Science and Innovation Writer 18:06, 14 Oct 2026 A car containing members of Salford's notorious A-Team gang drove-by the Walkden home Michelle Pearson and her children shared a month before a fatal petrol bomb attack claimed their li Four of her children - Demi, 15; Brandon, eight; Lacie, seven, and Lia, three - died in the attack carried out by Zak Bolland and David Worrall at around 5am on Monday, December 11, 2017. Ms Pearson died of her injuries in hospital 20 months later An inquest into their deaths at Bolton Coroners' Court has heard how Ms Pearson's 16-year-old son, Kyle, was involved in a tit-for-tat feud involving Bolland and others Today (October 14), the court was told Kyle raised concerns over a possible threat posed by the infamous A-Team gang weeks before Bolland and Worrall's attack. Ms Pearson had also reported threats from Bolland, who had demanded £500 from Kyle over a damaged vehicle During a visit to the family home by the Safeguarding Unit of Greater Manchester Police on November 28, 2017, the court heard how Ms Pearson also told officers she believed someone had phoned the A-Team and four males had driven past the house in a Silver Renault Clio

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Walkden Salford's A-Team gang 'drove by' Walkden house weeks before tragic fire-bombing, inquest hears Michelle Pearson and four of her children - Demi, Brandon, Lacie, and Lia - were killed in the attack in December 2017 View 7 Images (Image: MEN Med Add to preferred sources News Bethan Finighan Science and Innovation Writer 18:06, 14 Oct 2026 A car containing members of Salford's notorious A-Team gang drove-by the Walkden home Michelle Pearson and her children shared a month before a fatal petrol bomb attack claimed their li Four of her children - Demi, 15; Brandon, eight; Lacie, seven, and Lia, three - died in the attack carried out by Zak Bolland and David Worrall at around 5am on Monday, December 11, 2017. Ms Pearson died of her injuries in hospital 20 months later An inquest into their deaths at Bolton Coroners' Court has heard how Ms Pearson's 16-year-old son, Kyle, was involved in a tit-for-tat feud involving Bolland and others Today (October 14), the court was told Kyle raised concerns over a possible threat posed by the infamous A-Team gang weeks before Bolland and Worrall's attack. Ms Pearson had also reported threats from Bolland, who had demanded £500 from Kyle over a damaged vehicle During a visit to the family home by the Safeguarding Unit of Greater Manchester Police on November 28, 2017, the court heard how Ms Pearson also told officers she believed someone had phoned the A-Team and four males had driven past the house in a Silver Renault Clio

candidates.evidence_text: Salford This Greater Manchester area is home to some of the worst roads in the country The Greater Manchester area has scored high in national figures Add to preferred sources Comments News Ramazani Mwamba News reporter 06:01, 15 Oct 2026 View 2 Image The city of Salford is home to some of the worst roads in the country according to new figures released by the Department for Transport. A report lists locally-managed major roads that were reported in poor condition by their councils in the year to March 2026 In the UK, authorities are required to carry out regular surveys of surfaces they manage and categorise them as red, amber or green. Red being the highways that should have had major improvement Nationally, Salford Council was one of the authorities to record the highest proportion of poor roads with 13 per cent - that's a seven per cent increase from previous findings. On the list of shame, the city was only surpassed by Brent in London with 14 per cent, Nottingham with The closest authority to Salford in Greater Manchester was Manchester City Council who reported seven per cent, then Bury , Stockport , Wigan and Trafford with five per cent View 2 Images Salford is among one of the worst in the country (Image: Copyright Unknown)

Add to preferred sources Comments News Ramazani Mwamba News reporter 05:53, 15 Oct 2026 Updated 07:05, 15 Oct 202 A visitor to Manchester says he has been left 'helpless' and 'homeless' after his luxury city centre studio became infested with bedbugs The man, who asked to remain anonymous, told the Manchester Evening News of a nightmare experience at a flat in the Swan Street House complex in the Northern Quarter . A medical professional and originally from Birmingham, he travelled to work an study in the city After a fortnight in the region, he decided to book himself a short stay at the deluxe high-rise on Mason Street. He told the MEN his 12-day stay cost £1,634 when he booked it online. But after just one evening, he claims to have woke up with bug bites all over his body The property is understood to have offered the individual a refund since the incident. He said: "After the first day, I got a few rashes on my body so I went to the housekeeping and they came and changed my bedding "The second night it was more obvious, I thought there was something that doesn't look right. I called the housekeeping again and they did the same thing. But I wasn't convinced, I thought there was something more than that. So, I removed the mattress and it was full of bedbugs."

candidates.evidence_text: Bolton Man arrested after police seize over £340,000 worth of illegal vapes and drugs at Bolton properties The man has been arrested on suspicion of being concerned in the supply of class B drugs Add to preferred sources Comments News Charlotte Fisher A man has been arrested after police seized over £340,000 worth of illegal vapes, drugs, and suspected cannabis oil at two properties in Bolton earlier this week. The total value of the items is estimated to be over £349,700 It comes after officers from Greater Manchester Police , in partnership with Trading Standards and Bolton Council, raided two properties on Chorley Old Road and Bentinck Street on Monday (October 12) Over 25,000 single use vapes were seized, amounting to approximately £12,700 in street value, and over 3,500 bottles of vape liquid was also obtained Police also seized 500 bottles of suspected cannabis oil, valued at around £25,000, along with 100kg of CBD powder, estimated to be worth £60,000 The man, aged 45, has been arrested on suspicion of being concerned in the supply of class B drugs. He since been released on bail, pending further enquiries

candidates.evidence_text: Manchester Council 'There was no one like Pat Karney and there never will be again' A minute's silence was held in Manchester today for the late councillor Add to preferred sources Comments News Edward Barnes Local Democracy Reporter 20:10, 14 Oct 202 Described as a true one-off, he was a familiar face to generations of Mancunians and one of the city’s most prominent and well-known local politicians , serving as a councillor in Harpurhey from 1979. Coun Karney was also a champion and spokesperson for the Christmas Markets and A book of condolence was opened today at Manchester Central Library, where a flag will be flying at half-mast in tribute. Among those paying tribute today were Prime Minister Andy Burnham , who hailed him as 'a tireless champion for the people he represented.' Speaking to the Manchester Evening News , Manchester City Council leader Garry Bridges said the ‘huge outpouring of grief but also support for everything Pat did in his time in the city’ showed how highly regarded he was and his ‘extraordinary service’ He described the late councillor as someone who had ‘a real sense of fun but underneath it was deeply serious about his politics as well and the things that really mattered to him’ Pointing to times he brought out a chicken mask in the council chamber , Coun Bridges said: “When Pat picked up his carrier bag of tricks, you never knew exactly what was in it. We all look back with fondness now.”

candidates.evidence_text: Manchester Town Hall Danger warning as people told not to enter parts of Manchester Town Hall One warning sign in the building said: “Danger. Building works in progress. Do not enter.” Add to preferred sources Comments News Edward Barnes Local Democra Parts of Manchester town hall have been closed off after issues were found in the ceiling above the council chamber The chamber, which is in the Manchester Town Hall Extension, was built between 1934 and 1938. The building is Grade II* listed However parts of the building have been closed off to the public, though the Manchester Evening News understands the ceiling of the council chamber is not believed to be at risk of collapse One warning sign in the building said: “Danger. Building works in progress. Do not enter.” A Manchester City Council spokesperson said: “The council chamber is temporarily closed until a detailed inspection can be carried out. This follows the identification of slight irregularities in the ceiling and is purely a precautionary measure.”

candidates.evidence_text: Greater Manchester Police Warning issued as fraudsters impersonating police officers in 'incredibly sophisticated' crime Police have issued a warning following the rise of the 'incredibly sophisticated' scams Add to preferred sources Comments News Cha Police are urging people to remain vigilant as scammers impersonating police officers are targeting 'vulnerable communities' across Greater Manchester. The fraudsters are trying to convince victims to hand over personal and sensitive information The 'incredibly sophisticated type of crime' sees the scammers pretend to be police officers and ask victims about their cryptocurrency accounts A common method used by the fraudsters is to claim to be a suspect that has been arrested and found in possession of the victim's personal documents, such as their passport, driving licence or banking details. These calls can 'appear convincing' and are being made through fake GM The scammers have also asked victims about their cryptocurrency accounts on several occasions, specifically looking for their IDs, recovery phrases, and security codes. Officers would never ask anyone to share this information or move your accounts, GMP added DS Reed from our Cyber Crime Team said: "These calls are an incredibly sophisticated type of crime, and those responsible are targeting our vulnerable communities

candidates.evidence_text: Walkden Salford's A-Team gang 'drove by' Walkden house weeks before tragic fire-bombing, inquest hears Michelle Pearson and four of her children - Demi, Brandon, Lacie, and Lia - were killed in the attack in December 2017 View 7 Images (Image: MEN Med Add to preferred sources News Bethan Finighan Science and Innovation Writer 18:06, 14 Oct 2026 A car containing members of Salford's notorious A-Team gang drove-by the Walkden home Michelle Pearson and her children shared a month before a fatal petrol bomb attack claimed their li Four of her children - Demi, 15; Brandon, eight; Lacie, seven, and Lia, three - died in the attack carried out by Zak Bolland and David Worrall at around 5am on Monday, December 11, 2017. Ms Pearson died of her injuries in hospital 20 months later An inquest into their deaths at Bolton Coroners' Court has heard how Ms Pearson's 16-year-old son, Kyle, was involved in a tit-for-tat feud involving Bolland and others Today (October 14), the court was told Kyle raised concerns over a possible threat posed by the infamous A-Team gang weeks before Bolland and Worrall's attack. Ms Pearson had also reported threats from Bolland, who had demanded £500 from Kyle over a damaged vehicle During a visit to the family home by the Safeguarding Unit of Greater Manchester Police on November 28, 2017, the court heard how Ms Pearson also told officers she believed someone had phoned the A-Team and four males had driven past the house in a Silver Renault Clio

candidates.evidence_text: Irlam and Cadishead Irlam residents frustrated as they struggle to get off driveways Locals are left in fear of the proposed 154 new homes Add to preferred sources News Elizabeth Cotton TV and Celebrity Writer 17:58, 14 Oct 2026 View 2 Images Resident Residents in Irlam have said they are struggling to get off their own driveways because of traffic, as fears grow that plans for 154 new affordable homes will make congestion even worse People living in the area have taken to social media to share their frustration at the volume of vehicles on local roads, warning that the proposed development off Fiddlers Lane could add further pressure to an already busy road network Forshaw Land and Property Group has submitted a planning application to build 154 homes on a field off Fiddlers Lane, which is currently used for horse grazing. The proposals include 76 terraced houses and two apartment blocks containing a total of 78 flats All of the properties would be classed as affordable housing and made available through Salford City Council's Salford Homes Search. Housing association ForHousing would manage the homes once completed If approved, the development would feature a mix of two, three and four-bedroom houses, alongside one and two-bedroom flats. The plans also include a large public open space with native and ornamental trees, as well as parking, electric vehicle charging points and private gardens

The proposals include 76 terraced houses and two apartment blocks containing a total of 78 flats All of the properties would be classed as affordable housing and made available through Salford City Council's Salford Homes Search. Housing association ForHousing would manage the homes once completed If approved, the development would feature a mix of two, three and four-bedroom houses, alongside one and two-bedroom flats. The plans also include a large public open space with native and ornamental trees, as well as parking, electric vehicle charging points and private gardens

candidates.evidence_text: Middleton Unlicensed teen taught himself to drive on YouTube, ran red lights, then killed beloved dad in Middleton horror crash Ruhul Islam was sentenced to six years and 11 months in prison following the death of Terence James View 4 Images Ruhul Isl Add to preferred sources News Bethan Finighan Science and Innovation Writer 17:13, 14 Oct 2026 Updated 22:36, 14 Oct 2026 An unlicensed teenager who taught himself to drive by watching YouTube videos swerved through traffic and ran red lights before ploughing his older brother's Terence James , 78, died after being struck by the vehicle on Shawbury Street, Middleton , on September 29, 2024. Yesterday (October 13), Manchester Crown Court heard how Ruhul Islam had borrowed the car to make takeaway deliveries at the time of the offence The 16-year-old was seen overtaking and undertaking vehicles, running red lights and weaving between lanes in the moments before the crash Now 18, he has been jailed for nearly seven years. Passing sentence, Judge Kate Cornell said: "The vehicle essentially became a dangerous weapon in the hands of someone unable to use it." candidates.evidence_text: The last time I saw Pat Karney he was in great spirits “We all have to wear these now,” he said with a wry smile as he pointed to the Andy Burnham T-shirt beneath his tracksuit jacket. “They’re standard issue council uniform.” As he sat across the table from me at the Manchester Evening News ’ offices last month, he joked about how odd it was to see ‘Andy’ as Prime Minister and teased us about our extensive coverage of Mr Burnham these past few months I had asked him to visit the office to record a podcast about the origins of Manchester Pride - something Pat certainly knew a thing or two about as part of the trailblazing 1980s council who took on a homophobic police force “and won” View 6 Images Pat Karney has been known to generations of Mancunians (Image: MEN) But before I placed him in front of a microphone to wax lyrical, he took the time to encourage our new endeavour. “I think it’s great,” he said. “Keep going.” It was typically generous

english_fact_card.what_happened: A family home was smashed up and a severed pig's head was dumped on the front porch in Salford. At least four more houses were targeted on the evening of Tuesday, October 13, in Little Hulton, Walkden, and Kersley. Greater Manchester Police has confirmed a total of 25 incidents of criminal damage since October 5, treated as linked, with vandals targeting HMOs and properties mistaken for HMOs. One father was at home in Little Hulton when a gang of youths in balaclavas attacked the house next to his, then threw a brick through his front window.

english_fact_card.why_now: The vandalism is ongoing and being treated as linked by police, with 25 incidents reported since October 5.
english_fact_card.reader_value: Residents in Salford should be aware of the ongoing criminal damage and potential targeting of HMOs and similar properties.
english_fact_card.reader_action: Report any information to Greater Manchester Police; be vigilant if living in or near HMOs in the affected areas.

Add to preferred sources Comments News Ramazani Mwamba News reporter 05:53, 15 Oct 2026 Updated 07:05, 15 Oct 202 A visitor to Manchester says he has been left 'helpless' and 'homeless' after his luxury city centre studio became infested with bedbugs The man, who asked to remain anonymous, told the Manchester Evening News of a nightmare experience at a flat in the Swan Street House complex in the Northern Quarter . A medical professional and originally from Birmingham, he travelled to work an study in the city After a fortnight in the region, he decided to book himself a short stay at the deluxe high-rise on Mason Street. He told the MEN his 12-day stay cost £1,634 when he booked it online. But after just one evening, he claims to have woke up with bug bites all over his body The property is understood to have offered the individual a refund since the incident. He said: "After the first day, I got a few rashes on my body so I went to the housekeeping and they came and changed my bedding "The second night it was more obvious, I thought there was something that doesn't look right. I called the housekeeping again and they did the same thing. But I wasn't convinced, I thought there was something more than that. So, I removed the mattress and it was full of bedbugs."

candidates.evidence_text: Salford This Greater Manchester area is home to some of the worst roads in the country The Greater Manchester area has scored high in national figures Add to preferred sources Comments News Ramazani Mwamba News reporter 06:01, 15 Oct 2026 View 2 Image The city of Salford is home to some of the worst roads in the country according to new figures released by the Department for Transport. A report lists locally-managed major roads that were reported in poor condition by their councils in the year to March 2026 In the UK, authorities are required to carry out regular surveys of surfaces they manage and categorise them as red, amber or green. Red being the highways that should have had major improvement Nationally, Salford Council was one of the authorities to record the highest proportion of poor roads with 13 per cent - that's a seven per cent increase from previous findings. On the list of shame, the city was only surpassed by Brent in London with 14 per cent, Nottingham with The closest authority to Salford in Greater Manchester was Manchester City Council who reported seven per cent, then Bury , Stockport , Wigan and Trafford with five per cent View 2 Images Salford is among one of the worst in the country (Image: Copyright Unknown)

candidates.evidence_text: Bolton Man arrested after police seize over £340,000 worth of illegal vapes and drugs at Bolton properties The man has been arrested on suspicion of being concerned in the supply of class B drugs Add to preferred sources Comments News Charlotte Fisher A man has been arrested after police seized over £340,000 worth of illegal vapes, drugs, and suspected cannabis oil at two properties in Bolton earlier this week. The total value of the items is estimated to be over £349,700 It comes after officers from Greater Manchester Police , in partnership with Trading Standards and Bolton Council, raided two properties on Chorley Old Road and Bentinck Street on Monday (October 12) Over 25,000 single use vapes were seized, amounting to approximately £12,700 in street value, and over 3,500 bottles of vape liquid was also obtained Police also seized 500 bottles of suspected cannabis oil, valued at around £25,000, along with 100kg of CBD powder, estimated to be worth £60,000 The man, aged 45, has been arrested on suspicion of being concerned in the supply of class B drugs. He since been released on bail, pending further enquiries

Coun Karney was also a champion and spokesperson for the Christmas Markets and A book of condolence was opened today at Manchester Central Library, where a flag will be flying at half-mast in tribute. Among those paying tribute today were Prime Minister Andy Burnham , who hailed him as 'a tireless champion for the people he represented.' Speaking to the Manchester Evening News , Manchester City Council leader Garry Bridges said the ‘huge outpouring of grief but also support for everything Pat did in his time in the city’ showed how highly regarded he was and his ‘extraordinary service’ He described the late councillor as someone who had ‘a real sense of fun but underneath it was deeply serious about his politics as well and the things that really mattered to him’ Pointing to times he brought out a chicken mask in the council chamber , Coun Bridges said: “When Pat picked up his carrier bag of tricks, you never knew exactly what was in it. We all look back with fondness now.”

candidates.evidence_text: Greater Manchester Police Warning issued as fraudsters impersonating police officers in 'incredibly sophisticated' crime Police have issued a warning following the rise of the 'incredibly sophisticated' scams Add to preferred sources Comments News Cha Police are urging people to remain vigilant as scammers impersonating police officers are targeting 'vulnerable communities' across Greater Manchester. The fraudsters are trying to convince victims to hand over personal and sensitive information The 'incredibly sophisticated type of crime' sees the scammers pretend to be police officers and ask victims about their cryptocurrency accounts A common method used by the fraudsters is to claim to be a suspect that has been arrested and found in possession of the victim's personal documents, such as their passport, driving licence or banking details. Ms Pearson died of her injuries in hospital 20 months later An inquest into their deaths at Bolton Coroners' Court has heard how Ms Pearson's 16-year-old son, Kyle, was involved in a tit-for-tat feud involving Bolland and others Today (October 14), the court was told Kyle raised concerns over a possible threat posed by the infamous A-Team gang weeks before Bolland and Worrall's attack. candidates.evidence_text: Irlam and Cadishead Irlam residents frustrated as they struggle to get off driveways Locals are left in fear of the proposed 154 new homes Add to preferred sources News Elizabeth Cotton TV and Celebrity Writer 17:58, 14 Oct 2026 View 2 Images Resident Residents in Irlam have said they are struggling to get off their own driveways because of traffic, as fears grow that plans for 154 new affordable homes will make congestion even worse People living in the area have taken to social media to share their frustration at the volume of vehicles on local roads, warning that the proposed development off Fiddlers Lane could add further pressure to an already busy road network Forshaw Land and Property Group has submitted a planning application to build 154 homes on a field off Fiddlers Lane, which is currently used for horse grazing. The proposals include 76 terraced houses and two apartment blocks containing a total of 78 flats All of the properties would be classed as affordable housing and made available through Salford City Council's Salford Homes Search. Housing association ForHousing would manage the homes once completed If approved, the development would feature a mix of two, three and four-bedroom houses, alongside one and two-bedroom flats. The plans also include a large public open space with native and ornamental trees, as well as parking, electric vehicle charging points and private gardens

candidates.evidence_text: Manchester Airport Salford dad slams 'crazy' Manchester Airport system as he's hit with £100 fine - but they say he ignored 'important rule' He has hit out at the autopay system at Manchester Airport, but they have defended the fine Add to preferred s A man has slammed Manchester Airport after his wife was issued a £100 fine - despite their car being registered for automatic payments at drop-off zones. Michael Joseph said the fine 'undermines the autopay system' after they were charged for dropping their son off at the airport The Airport says they overstayed the 15 minute limit, hence the charge. Michael, 52, said his partner took their son to the Terminal 2 pick-up zone on September 23. The family, from Salford , previously set up autopay after having 'a bad experience with parking at the airport' The system allows people to register their vehicle online with a payment card and be automatically charged for pick-ups or drop-offs at the airport If drivers don't have autopay set up, they have to visit Manchester Airport's website - or call up - to pay charges by midnight the day after visits. Missing the payment deadline results in a £100 Parking Charge Notice View 4 Images They received the fine despite having an AutoPay account (Image: Manchester Evening News)

Officers served a Closure Notice on the premises following an investigation sparked by years of intelligence gathering and concerns from local residents and businesses Officers from Greater Manchester Police's Oldham Neighbourhood Team carried out a warrant at a premises on Broadway at around 4.45am on Wednesday, October 14 The operation was led by Neighbourhood Inspector Amie Whitehead and Police Sergeant Tom Layton, with support from the Tactical Aid Unit The warrant was secured after officers seized a mobile phone during an unrelated arrest of a man believed to be connected to the business. Investigators examining the device uncovered evidence that suggested the premises was being used to control prostitution During the raid, officers found a woman in her 40s at the address. Credit: UK Parliament A Labour MP has revealed that she is a victim of domestic abuse - Speaking in the Commons on October 13, Kirith Entwistle, who represents Bolton North East, described her experience of the current court system as "triggering", adding that she had to watch her abuser "stare at her" during a recent video hearing Ms Entwistle told her fellow MPs that she believes special measures - where victims are given protection or assistance in court - should be the standard in cases involving domestic abuse Examples of these measures could include screens, the ability to give evidence through a live link, or witnesses being able to be accompanied when giving evidence Measures to protect victims are included in the Courts and Tribunals Bill, which is currently going through Parliament Speaking during a debate on the bill, Ms Entwistle said: "It doesn’t matter how many times somebody tells me that they understand what I’m going through, or they acknowledge what I’ve been through, they really don’t unless they have lived it themselves or know somebody who has."

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Saturday 1 August 2026 at 3:57pm The Prime Minister celebrated with the new Mayor in Manchester on Saturday morning. Credit: PA Images Andy Burnham told his successor as Greater Manchester mayor to “go further and do more” as he dubbed her the “queen of the north” after her by-el Labour candidate Bev Craig won the largest by-election in British history to succeed Mr Burnham in the job after he quit and became Prime Minister The result was announced late on Friday night, more than 24 hours after polling stations closed, in a comfortable win, although with a low turnout Speaking at a victory event in Manchester alongside Ms Craig, Mr Burnham touted his plans to further devolve power out of Westminster “So, here’s my challenge to you today. On the back of that, I’m afraid you’re just going to have to go further and do more,” he said

She’s wearing Musera, which looks to be Manchester’s friendliest, chicest new clothing label — launched in 2024 from an From this Newton Street office, a band of young designers turn out a stream of trend pieces: low-rise trousers and asymmetric tops, distressed knitwear and leopard-print flares, western fringed jumpers and A-level prom gowns. Their Instagram bio lauds the brand as “Est. MCR.” Over a million people watched the staff dancing around their Northern Quarter office to Whigfield’s Saturday Night on TikTok. More still tuned in to a video showing them kitted out in Musera for Drake’s performance at Co-op Live last year. And who knows how many have sidestepped “Be a muse in your own era,” goes their slogan; presumably also the source of their similarly recondite name. Their Instagram captions are a list of internet cliches verging on parody. “My blood type is iced latte,” reads one post Looking at this well-curated online presence, you might well be convinced that Musera is, as they suggest, Manchester through and through

evidence_packet.evidence_text: How a sweatshop empire is Manchester-washing its reputation “I can’t always be in LA,” reads one TikTok caption, “someone has to hold it down in Rochdale.” It’s written over a model strutting through a leatherwear shoot. She’s wearing Musera, which looks to be Manchester’s friendliest, chicest new clothing label — launched in 2024 from an From this Newton Street office, a band of young designers turn out a stream of trend pieces: low-rise trousers and asymmetric tops, distressed knitwear and leopard-print flares, western fringed jumpers and A-level prom gowns. Their Instagram bio lauds the brand as “Est. MCR.” Over a million people watched the staff dancing around their Northern Quarter office to Whigfield’s Saturday Night on TikTok. More still tuned in to a video showing them kitted out in Musera for Drake’s performance at Co-op Live last year. And who knows how many have sidestepped “Be a muse in your own era,” goes their slogan; presumably also the source of their similarly recondite name. Their Instagram captions are a list of internet cliches verging on parody. “My blood type is iced latte,” reads one post Looking at this well-curated online presence, you might well be convinced that Musera is, as they suggest, Manchester through and through

Many junior staff members believe raising issues will lead to retaliation, and 59% of survey respondents have witnessed or experienced a form of harassment, discrimi One worker recalled a young apprentice being repeatedly sexually harassed by a senior colleague until she was forced to leave the council. “He was allowed to stay,” they said of the offending staffer. “She was interviewed by two male managers and needless to say she left.” There A council worker, speaking to us on the condition of anonymity, said of the report: “if I were a manager that would sicken me to my core.” When we approached the council before publishing this story, CEO Tom Stannard said: “it is completely unacceptable that anyone should feel undervalued, unable to raise concerns, unsupported if they do or – in the worst cases – unsafe. These issues cannot and will not be ignored.”

candidates.evidence_text: Plans submitted for £800,000 gym and wellbeing facilities at Altrincham office building Skip to content News — Property Plans submitted for £800,000 gym and wellbeing facilities at Altrincham office building Station House has been part of Altrincham's townscape since 1966. , and David Prior October 14, 2026 . 12:44 PM 2 min read Share on Twitter Share on Facebook Share on Pinterest Share on LinkedIn Share on WhatsApp Share via Email Property company Bruntwood has submitted plans for a new £800,000 gym and wellbeing facility at Station House in Altrincham town centre. The proposals would see part of the existing ground-floor undercroft at the office building, next to Altrincham Interchange, transformed into a 1,200 sq ft fitness space for businesses based there. If approved, the investment would create a high-spec gym alongside new showering, changing and wellbeing facilities, designed to make it easier for people to exercise or cycle to work. The facilities would include five showers, including one accessible shower, lockers, a drying cupboard and a towel drop. There would also be vanity areas equipped with hairdryers and straighteners, while landscaping improvements at the front and rear of the building would provide a more welcoming entrance for workers and visitors. The plans represent the latest stage in Bruntwood Places' ongoing investment in Station House, which is celebrating its 60th anniversary this year. The building has been a fixture of Altrincham town centre since 1966 and is now home to more than 50 businesses, including Civica, Zelus Sport, Rise Fibre and London Care. As Altrincham Today reported in July , Bruntwood Places has recently completed major refurbishments of the building's first and sixth floors. Bruntwood Places has recently completed refurbishments of the first and sixth floors The sixth floor, which includes nine serviced offices, four conventional workspaces, two meeting rooms and private phone booths, is now fully let. The newly refurbished first floor provides a further six conventional and eight serviced office suites, along with three phone booths. Station House offers everything from pay-as-you-go coworking desks to fully managed private offices, with facilities including a communal lounge, meeting rooms, bike storage and 24-hour access. Its reception, lift lobbies and toilets have also been upgraded as part of the wider programme of improvements. Sharon Johnson, Head of Commercial at Bruntwood, said: “We know the best workspaces need to offer much more than a desk. People increasingly want their working environment to support their wellbeing, give them flexibility in how they spend their day and make it easier to balance work with the things that matter outside it. Station House is home to more than 50 businesses “Our plans for Station House are about responding to those changing expectations, by investing in high-quality fitness and wellbeing facilities alongside flexible offices and shared spaces to meet and connect. “Its position at the heart of one of the North West’s most dynamic and sought-after town centres makes it a go-to destination for ambitious businesses looking to grow and succeed, while bringing people into the heart of Altrincham to be part of its thriving local community.” The proposals are the latest investment in Altrincham by Bruntwood, which is also involved in the ongoing regeneration of Stamford Quarter in partnership with Trafford Council. The planning application has now been submitted to Trafford Council for consideration. candidates.evidence_text: It's one of the longest-running sagas in the town Share on WhatsApp Share via Email One of Altrincham's longest-running regeneration sagas could be entering a new chapter, with Trafford Council proposing to turn the former Altair site into a major residential development The council is recommending that the 4.5-acre site between Oakfield Road and Moss Lane should be developed primarily for housing, potentially bringing an end to almost two decades of failed plans for a major new shopping, leisure and residential quarter The proposals, which will be considered by Trafford Council's Executive on Monday October 19, would also see the existing surface car park potentially replaced by a multi-storey parking and transport hub An indicative masterplan includes apartment buildings of five storeys or more, smaller residential blocks, commercial space and landscaped communal areas The plans represent a significant change of direction for the site, which was originally earmarked for the £70 million Altair development first unveiled in 2008

candidates.evidence_text: North Cestrian School is expanding into the former Loreto Preparatory School site Share on WhatsApp Share via Email Plans to create up to 300 additional secondary school places in Altrincham have taken a significant step forward with the appointment of a contractor to oversee the next phase of the project Trafford Council has appointed construction firm Tilbury Douglas to work on the proposed expansion of North Cestrian School into the former Loreto Preparatory School site The council announced in August that it had purchased the neighbouring site, paving the way for the school to expand and help meet growing demand for secondary school places in the area Tilbury Douglas has now been appointed under a Pre-Construction Services Agreement (PCSA), which will see the company work with Trafford Council, Hamblin Education Trust and the design team to develop the scheme ahead of the construction phase The proposed expansion would allow North Cestrian to accommodate up to 300 additional pupils, helping more Altrincham children secure places at a local secondary school

candidates.evidence_text: The Altrincham line will be closed again between Monday October 19 and Sunday November 1 Share on WhatsApp Share via Email Transport for Greater Manchester has announced a major change to its plans for the upcoming Altrincham Metrolink closure , with direct shuttle buses now set to operate between Altrincham and Manchester city centre The move comes after TfGM initially confirmed that no dedicated replacement buses would serve Altrincham, Navigation Road or Timperley during the two-week shutdown from Monday October 19 to Sunday November 1 Instead, passengers were told to use the existing 263 bus service or trains into Manchester, with replacement buses operating only between Sale and the city centre But in a welcome change of plan, TfGM has now confirmed that a new non-stop shuttle service will run directly between Altrincham and Piccadilly every 15 minutes The service will operate between 7am and 7pm during the closure, although a detailed timetable has yet to be published

Richardson, of no fixed address, denies both murder and manslaughter

candidates.summary: Three people were seriously injured when the double-decker bus struck a low bridge on Barton Lane in Eccles in July 2025, tearing off its roof One victim suffered a fractured skull and several others were hurt after being ejected from the top deck Christopher Henry was sentenced

candidates.lead: Three people were seriously injured when the double-decker bus struck a low bridge on Barton Lane in Eccles in July 2025, tearing off its roof One victim suffered a fractured skull and several others were hurt after being ejected from the top deck Christopher Henry was sentenced
candidates.evidence_text: Three people were seriously injured when the double-decker bus struck a low bridge on Barton Lane in Eccles in July 2025, tearing off its roof One victim suffered a fractured skull and several others were hurt after being ejected from the top deck Christopher Henry was sentenced to two years and eight months, suspended for two-and-a-half years, after admitting causing serious injury by dangerous driving Manchester Crown Court heard Henry ignored several low bridge warnings after taking a wrong turn while driving the 100 service between the Trafford Centre and Manchester city centre The court heard the experienced driver appeared to be driving on "autopilot" after earlier operating the single-decker 52 service, which uses Barton Lane, and may have believed he was still on that route Henry was also ordered to complete 300 hours of unpaid work and pay £150 in costs. He was banned from driving for two years and must pass an extended re-test before regaining his licence

evidence_texts: A mural has been created to honour the legacy of an anti-crime campaigner who was inspired to act after her son's death Patsy McKie's youngest son Dorrie, 20, was shot dead in the Hulme area of Manchester in 1999 Just days later, she co-founded Mothers Against Violence (MAVUK) and dedicated the rest of her life to travelling across the world to raise awareness of her anti-crime campaign A colourful mural, created by artist Marcus Lane, has been painted at the MAVUK Hulme Centre following her death in January 2025 at the age of 77 "She was a very bright person, even through some of the most difficult periods of her life," said her son, Ian Swanston "She wanted to bring a sense of colour to the world

Patsy McKie's youngest son Dorrie, 20, was shot dead in the Hulme area of Manchester in 1999 Just days later, she co-founded Mothers Against Violence (MAVUK) and dedicated the rest of her life to travelling across the world to raise awareness of her anti-crime campaign A colourful mural, created by artist Marcus Lane, has been painted at the MAVUK Hulme Centre following her death in January 2025 at the age of 77 "She was a very bright person, even through some of the most difficult periods of her life," said her son, Ian Swanston "She wanted to bring a sense of colour to the world "A creative artwork representing Patsy would have to be colourful, because that's definitely what she wants."

candidates.lead: In 2028 it will be 100 years since women were granted the right to vote on equal terms with men
candidates.evidence_text: In 2028 it will be 100 years since women were granted the right to vote on equal terms with men Although some women were granted the right to vote in 1918, it was not until 1928 that all women over the age of 21 were granted the vote regardless of their occupation, wealth or ownership of property To mark this hugely significant milestone a Council motion has been set out to recognise and celebrate this moment in history It is no secret that Manchester played a huge part in the Women’s Suffrage movement. The Pankhurst name is known across the globe and is a byword for resilience and a refusal to give in to apparent insurmountable odds In 2018 a statue of Emmeline Pankhurst was proudly installed in St Peter’s Square and has since become a rallying point for people across the city to have their voices heard, and acts as a powerful reminder that history was made by women who refused to give up But the Pankhursts were also joined by thousands of ordinary Mancunian women whose names have been lost to history, but whose legacy still lives on a century later

candidates.evidence_text: From the fabulous Feast of Fire celebrations to the iconic Christmas Lights Switch-On, the town centre will host an exciting calendar of entertainment as the Greater Manchester Town of Culture 2026 The programme will showcase the very best of Oldham's culture, creativity and community spirit with a series of free family-friendly events The programme begins with the Feast of Fire event on Saturday 31 October 2026. A joint celebration of Halloween and Bonfire Night, this spellbinding event will light up the heart of the town centre with fire dance performances and The Lips Halloween Show by Puppets with Guts foll Then, just two weeks later, the festive season will officially begin with the Oldham Christmas Lights Switch-On on Saturday 14 November. The day will start with a family-focused programme from 1pm featuring meet and greets with Peppa Pig, appearances from Oldham's mascots and act The celebrations will continue into the evening with the big Switch On Show from 5.30pm featuring Father Christmas, Peppa Pig's Dance Party, Oldham Rock Choir and performances from Fierce Dance The Mayor of Oldham Cllr Pam Byrne will also take part in the celebrations before a local school child competition winner will switch on the town's Christmas lights. The evening will conclude with a festive fireworks finale, accompanied by a lights and laser show

candidates.evidence_text: Oldham Council has secured a court order requiring the removal of an unauthorised encampment from Oldham Edge Council officers first visited the site on Thursday 6th August following concerns from residents and people using the park. Officers spoke to those at the encampment, who said they intended to leave by Saturday 8th August As the site had not been vacated, the Council returned with support from Greater Manchester Police on Tuesday 11th August. A formal direction was served under Section 77 of the Criminal Justice and Public Order Act 1994, requiring those at the encampment to leave and remove their The Council also provided information about authorised sites in Greater Manchester, along with advice about health, wellbeing and reporting hate crime After the direction was not followed, the Council began court proceedings. On Monday 17th August, Tameside Magistrates’ Court granted an order requiring the removal of the encampment The site was vacated later that day. A significant amount of waste was left behind, which has now been removed by the Council’s cleansing team

candidates.evidence_text: Libraries across the borough are teaming up with a local charity to help families access thousands of free pre-loved school uniforms and shoes As families continue to manage the high costs of school uniform, households cannot always afford the necessary items needed for their child This has led to growing demand for affordable alternatives, including a reliance on local charities like Uniform For All, which Rochdale Borough Council is working with to support those who need extra help Every day high-quality pre-loved items, including polo shirts, skirts, trousers, branded school blazers, coats and pumps, are given to families through the charity However, not every family has the resources to travel long distances to collect their orders That is why Rochdale’s library service is helping to collect these items so families can pick them up closer to where they live at their nearest library and save on additional travel costs

candidates.evidence_text: A week of action will challenge common misconceptions about Pension Credit, as government estimates show 35% of eligible pensioners are not claiming their full entitlement Bolton Council is using Pension Credit Week of Action (12-16 October) to raise awareness and to ensure that everyone who can claim, does claim There are between 760,000 and 910,000 eligible households who fail to claim Pension Credit which means up to £2.5bn goes unclaimed each year In some areas, the number of eligible households failing to claim is as high as 50% Many pensioners may be unaware of Pension Credit, or assume by owning their own home, being employed, having savings or receiving a private pension this will disqualify them from receiving it Bolton Council and a wide range of cost-of-living support groups are urging people to check out if they are entitled to Pension Credit as potentially it is worth up to £4,300 a year per claimant

candidates.evidence_text: Young people from across the borough came together to explore how our collective green journeys can create a more sustainable future for all Organised by Wigan Council’s Climate Response team, the Youth Climate Summit returned to The Edge for the fifth time on Wednesday, 30th September, bringing together pupils from primary schools, secondary schools, and colleges for an event focusing on this year’s theme of green jo The theme encouraged attendees to think about their own path to sustainability, how they can make better choices, and how we can all work together to find solutions to the climate crisis Councillor Paul Kenny, portfolio holder for planning, environmental service, and transport, said: “It’s fantastic that so many young people at the Youth Climate Summit came together to learn about sustainability and how they can have a positive impact on the environment “The green journeys theme is particularly important as it highlights that although we may all start at different places, or follow different paths, we can all work towards a common goal “That common goal should be how we can improve people’s lives, find solutions to the climate crisis, and ensure our planet is habitable for generations to come, and it was inspiring to see so many young people engaging with this important message.”

candidates.lead: Experience the raw, unfiltered power of Balkan folklore in a new immersive show from the world’s most famous performance artist Balkan Erotic Epic is a bold new performance work created by the iconic artist Marina Abramović .
candidates.evidence_text: Experience the raw, unfiltered power of Balkan folklore in a new immersive show from the world’s most famous performance artist Balkan Erotic Epic is a bold new performance work created by the iconic artist Marina Abramović . Regarded as the world’s most influential performance artist, Abramović’s transformative work has reached millions of people – from opening the Pyramid Stage at Glastonbury Festival t A four-hour ritual where ancient myth meets performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic explores the eroticism, spirituality and traditions of Abramović’s homeland through 13 visceral scenes Brought to life by a cast of over 70 performers, dancers, musicians and singers, the experience unfolds across Aviva Studios. Audiences are free to choose their own path – with pop-up encounters punctuating the action, bringing bodies together in dance, song and ritual Watch Fertility Rite , a fevered ritual where bodies writhe against the ground in a desperate call for fertility. Witness Massaging the Breast where women gesticulate over graves to awaken the earth. In Scaring the Gods , women bare themselves to the sky to banish storms. Listen Unafraid to push the boundaries of eroticism and performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic asks its audience a timeless question: What are our bodies truly for?

History, power and empire collide in Button Up! – a major new exhibition from the world-leading artist and activist Ai Weiwei . Internationally renowned artist and activist Ai Weiwei turns his critical gaze to the last 200 years of global history with this major new exhibition. Monumental in scale and ambition, Ai Weiwei: Button Up! is the artist’s most expansive presentation in the North to date.. Ai Weiwei is known around the world for his uncompromising artistic vision and political activism. From a childhood in exile to surviving secret detention in China, his remarkable life and career have led him to global prominence. Using sculpture, installation, film, photography and architecture, his work is unafraid to ask urgent, critical questions.. In Button Up! , the artist turns his lens on two centuries of Chinese and British relations. Taking inspiration from Manchester, a city at the heart of the Industrial Revolution, Button Up! explores how historic systems of trade, empire and exploitation resonate in today’s humanitarian and political crises.. Conceived as a total environment, Ai Weiwei: Button Up! brings together new and existing large-scale works on display in the UK for the first time. The monumental installation features porcelain, cotton, glass, bronze and even buttons and toy bricks. Each material contains a story of human invention and consumption. Together, they paint a picture of globalisation.. Both global and personal, the title Button Up! is a playful poke at the artist’s ongoing battle with censorship. The exhibition also features the world premiere of a new body of work created especially for the vast spaces of the Warehouse – Eight-Nation Alliance Flags made from millions of buttons, as well as a new version of History Of Bombs made entirely from toy bricks.. The new commissions sit alongside large-scale works by the artist which are going on show in the UK for the first time: Law of the Journey (2017), a 47m long inflatable migrant boat containing hundreds of human figures and the artist’s largest artwork to date; Wang Family Ancestral Hall (2015), a Ming dynasty ancestral temple reassembled from 1,500 individual wooden pieces ; and La Commedia Umana (2017-21), a black Murano glass chandelier made up of over 2,000 pieces and weighing nearly 3 tonnes. Also on show is Circle of Animals/Zodiac Heads (2010), a re-envisioning of the twelve animals of the Chinese zodiac.. Button Up! immerses visitors in Ai Weiwei’s fearless interrogation of the forces past and present that drive today’s injustices – while championing art’s enduring power to challenge and inspire.. . . . “I’m not interested in making very big things just for the sake of it. But in Manchester, that wonderful Warehouse space calls for monumental work. Visiting the city for this exhibition – the birthplace of the Industrial Revolution – and reflecting on Britain’s global territorial expansion made me realise I had to explore that history and understand how it connects to the forces driving today’s wars and global crises. The world today is deeply divided, with tragedy all around. Understanding history goes hand in hand with standing up for truth and justice.”. Ai Weiwei. . . Explore. . Ai Weiwei | Dream Space . candidates.evidence_text: Finish work and unwind with live music from Manchester’s best jazz musicians. Beat the Jams live series showcases the very best of the jazz scene, at short rush hour gigs from 6pm at Band on the Wall. What better way to avoid those endless queues, chaotic traffic and stressful homeward journeys? Clock off and skip the rush-hour traffic while you watch live jazz and make the most of our happy hour deals from 5–7pm: £4.50 pints / 2 for £15 cocktails / £15 bottles of wine + pizzas from £5! The new season kicks off on 24 September with tenor saxophonist Dean Masser and pianist Richard Wetherall, followed by: 7 October – Anna Chandler-King Quartet Leeds based saxophonist and composer Anna joins us again for Beat the Jams, this time with her own band. Anna’s thoughtful and inventive compositions are firm favourites of us at Beat the Jams and her quartet promises to be a unique rush hour busting treat! 16 November – Sam Lightwing Quartet Saxophonist and composer Sam Lightwing brings presents brand new music for his thrilling young quartet, showcasing Sam’s original compositions, which blend classic mainstream jazz grooves with modern flavours of post-pop and latin, all wrapped up in the language of contemporary sax giants such as Chris Potter, Seamus Blake and Joshua Redman. 15 December – Svarc/Devine/Walsh with Richard Iles The band combines deep pocket, fearless interplay and a shared love of exploration. Expect everything from soulful melodies and infectious rhythms to moments of exhilarating collective improvisation, delivered with the chemistry that only world-class musicians can create. Tickets from £13 per show, or £42 for a season ticket

Whether your child already attends our Saturday Music Club, or just wants to try something new, our Young Musician’s Summer School is suitable for all abilities!
