The course will conclude with a live performance soundtracking the film for family and friends. We welcome all abilities and instruments to take part in this course. You can bring your own instruments, but we have keyboards, guitars, bass, violins, drums and percussion on site which can be used if you don’t have an instrument. From ancient airs to future soundscapes, The Olllam is not just carrying the tradition forward—they’re reinventing it

candidates.evidence_text: An immersive celebration of the greatest songs from the movies and the joy of singing together Gareth Malone – the man who got the nation singing – is back on the road this autumn with Sing-A-Long-A-Gareth: At The Movies , a brand-new live show celebrating the unforgettable songs that have helped make movie moments magical Following the success of last year’s singalong tour, which saw thousands of people across the country fill theatres with song, laughter and joy, Gareth now turns his attention to the big screen. From sweeping cinema classics to feel-good favourites, At The Movies will bring audie Gareth Malone is a fellow of the Royal Academy of Music where he studied with Janice Chapman and Jonathan Papp. He was awarded an honorary doctorate from the University of East Anglia and Freedom of the City of London in 2010. In 2012 he was made OBE in the Queen’s birthday honou He first appeared on TV in the three-part BAFTA award-winning series The Choir for BBC, tackling the task of teaching choral singing to people who have never had the chance, or experience to sing before. Followed by three further series; The Choir: Boys Don’t Sing, The Choir: Uns The end time for this event is tbc. More details will be published nearer to the event

candidates.evidence_text: This year's nominations for Manchester's best bar, best restaurant and best chef are now open Go to Manchester's Finest X profile The Manchester Food and Drink Festival (MFDF) Awards have revealed their 2026 shortlists, with some of Greater Manchester’s best-known restaurants, bars, pubs, cafés and independent food businesses among the nominees The awards ceremony will take place on Monday 25 January 2027, moving to City Hall at Medlock Square for the first time. Big screens will bring the biggest sporting matches to The opening will bring one of the town centre’s biggest units back to life, creating around 140 jobs and giving Wigan a brand new day-to-night venue. It joins a growing STACK family that started in Newcastle in 2018 and now spans venues from Seaburn and Lincoln to Middlesbrough The six food traders confirmed for STACK Wigan have now been revealed, with Pattersons , Acropolis , ZZA Pizzeria , Tikka Bros , Smash House and Hello Oriental bringing everything from fried chicken and Greek gyros to stonebaked pizza, Indian street food, smash burgers and pan-As Tikka Bros is a homegrown Wigan name, having opened its first outlet in the town centre before expanding to Southport Market. Bringing a second site to Wigan with STACK, the Indian street food brand will serve fresh, tandoor-cooked dishes from Tikka Flame Bites to its loaded Smas

Big screens will bring the biggest sporting matches to The opening will bring one of the town centre’s biggest units back to life, creating around 140 jobs and giving Wigan a brand new day-to-night venue. It joins a growing STACK family that started in Newcastle in 2018 and now spans venues from Seaburn and Lincoln to Middlesbrough The six food traders confirmed for STACK Wigan have now been revealed, with Pattersons , Acropolis , ZZA Pizzeria , Tikka Bros , Smash House and Hello Oriental bringing everything from fried chicken and Greek gyros to stonebaked pizza, Indian street food, smash burgers and pan-As Tikka Bros is a homegrown Wigan name, having opened its first outlet in the town centre before expanding to Southport Market. Bringing a second site to Wigan with STACK, the Indian street food brand will serve fresh, tandoor-cooked dishes from Tikka Flame Bites to its loaded Smas

candidates.evidence_text: L-R: Simon Shaw, Anna Dick, Alastair Brown, Tripti Anil, Alan Jackson Simon Shaw, Delivery Director at Codurance, hosted the lunchtime session for tech leaders and introduced Codurance, which is a global software engineering consultancy that has run its Manchester office for 15 years He was joined on the panel by Anna Dick, Chief Technology & Product Officer at Capsule; Alastair Brown, Group Director of AI and Technology at Peninsula; Tripti Anil, Senior Leader, Data & Analytics at Kellanova; and Alan Jackson, Director of Client Solutions at Codurance Talking about discovering how AI can be used in projects, Anna said that Capsule's initial three months of AI exploration across all its business teams built appetite for further experimentation, but it also got a little out of control. Some things needed revisiting and tidying u Alastair stressed product discipline in order to understand the business driver and the outcome you want. At Peninsula, one initiative focused on giving customers richer answers and delivered over £1m in revenue. He also confirmed that AI will be a central focus of the That felt particularly relevant following an event we hosted through the UK Tech Cluster Group with AI Minister Kanishka Narayan, North East Mayor Kim McGuinness and other regional leaders, looking at AI, devolution and local growth One of the clearest themes from the discussion was that devolution should not mean every place trying to build the same thing. Different regions have different strengths, assets and specialisms, and there was a strong view that greater collaboration between places could create bi Procurement and buying local also featured strongly. The discussion highlighted the role public sector buying power can play in supporting regional businesses, helping successful pilots move into commercial contracts and strengthening UK capability in areas such as AI and cyber There was also a broader conversation about sovereignty and the UK’s role internationally. The discussion was not about trying to own every part of the AI stack, but about understanding where the UK already has genuine capability and where it makes sense to build more. Strengths

candidates.lead: Tech investment isn't slowing down, but the pattern of investment is changing.
candidates.evidence_text: Tech investment isn't slowing down, but the pattern of investment is changing. As investors grow increasingly selective, the capital ecosystem has become polarised. More capital is being concentrated in fewer companies while the market for exits remains difficult Financial news recently added another dimension to that discussion. AI-related shares fell last week after Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei called for a slower approach to the development of increasingly capable AI models. Nvidia finished the day down 3.4%, SoftBank fell 10.7% in Tokyo Additionally, the Bank of England is predicted to increase interest rates later this year, which could affect the North West's tech funding landscape by raising the cost of capital across the board, compressing valuations, pushing investors toward profitability over growth-at-all The British Business Bank's 2026 Small Business Equity Tracker found that equity investment into UK smaller businesses fell 4% to £12.3bn in 2025. Seed deal numbers fell 27% and venture deals fell 13%. AI companies attracted 44% of all investment into smaller businesses while the Beauhurst recorded £14.4bn of UK equity investment across 2,799 deals in the first half of 2026 but three AI companies accounted for 29% of all the capital raised. Those very large rounds can make the overall market look stronger than it feels to businesses raising at seed or Ser Beauhurst's analysis shows that UK equity investment more than doubled between 2017 and 2021 to £32.2bn while annual exits remained at around 400 to 500. An exit takes a median of four years from a funding round

Here, they share their perspectives on the trends they believe will have the greatest impact, the opportunities and challenges ahead, and what organisations should be thinking about now to stay ready for the future Part One , featuring more perspectives from across the ecosystem, can be read here MD Future 26 is sponsored by Pulsant , Novacoast with Platform Markets Group and CTI Digital , with support from Department and UK Tech Cluster Group

candidates.lead: Software engineered in Stoke-on-Trent and Manchester has secured another five years in one of Europe’s most tightly regulated digital markets.
candidates.evidence_text: Stoke-built software wins five more years in the Netherlands Posted on October 14, 2026 by staff Software built in Stoke and Manchester wins five more years in the Netherlands Code written by Hillside Technology's teams in Stoke and Manchester has cleared a five-year Dutch renewal. Why compliance engineering is now an export product Share: Listen to article Partner content Software engineered in Stoke-on-Trent and Manchester has secured another five years in one of Europe’s most tightly regulated digital markets. For the North’s tech scene, the renewal says something about what the region now exports: platforms built to pass an inspection in a country their developers may never visit. A northern engineering base The software belongs to bet365, founded in 2000 in North Staffordshire. By 2023 it employed more than 6,000 people and operated in 21 languages, figures the company gave when its technology arm, Hillside Technology, set up a Platform Innovation Hub to test new tools against the core platform. Manchester came first, in 2016. The firm opened its first satellite technology office in Spring Gardens, hiring 50 to 70 people to support the development teams in Stoke-on-Trent. Dom Hawley, then head of software development, said at the time that bet365 had found exceptional people in Stoke but now had to recruit outside the local area to keep growing. BusinessCloud covered the move into Manchester when it was announced. A year later the Spring Gardens office was set to grow from 60 to more than 150 staff , with developers in both cities building the HTML5 desktop site together. Testing followed. In late 2022 Hillside brought its software testing academy to Manchester , hiring up to 10 testers on aptitude rather than CV and training them toward the ISTQB Certified Tester Foundation Level. In a regulated product, testing carries more weight than usual. Every market the platform enters adds a rule set, and somebody has to prove the software obeys it. A licence that has to be earned twice On 17 September the Kansspelautoriteit (KSA), the Netherlands’ regulator for games of chance, announced its first eight follow-up licences . One went to Hillside (New Media Malta) Plc, the bet365 company that holds the Dutch permit. The original licences date from 2021, when the Dutch market opened, and expired at the end of September 2026. The renewals run from October 2026 to September 2031. It was no rubber stamp. The KSA says this round was the first where it looked explicitly at violations confirmed over the previous five years. Applicants had to explain what they had done to fix them and how they would stop them happening again, and the regulator handed some of them extra points for attention without naming which. A platform built in Stoke does not carry its British approval abroad. It re-qualifies country by country, against each regulator’s rules and, in the Dutch case, against its own record. Repeat that across every jurisdiction and the result is a set of separate licensed pools, each defined by one regulator’s register and most of them far smaller than Britain’s. Because each pool has a hard edge, the gap can be counted. The count in Casino.net’s online casino reviews across 17 markets shows how steep it is: 103 reviews of UKGC-licensed operators, against 13 for Malta’s MGA, 11 for Germany’s GGL, 10 for Spain’s DGOJ and 9 for AGCO-registered operators in Ontario. The Netherlands, where bet365 has just renewed, still sits at “final checks” there, one of nine markets in progress. Compliance as the product For engineers in Stoke and Manchester, those numbers describe the job. A UK build serves a crowded market under one rulebook. A Dutch, German or Ontario build serves a much thinner field under a different one, with its own limits and its own data feeds to the regulator. The Dutch renewal included a fresh integration test of the link to the KSA’s control database. None of it is visible to a customer, and all of it has to work on day one. It also has to keep working when the rules change mid-licence, which in the Netherlands they did on 1 January 2026, when the KSA added new requirements, among them an exit plan, ahead of this renewal round. It is also expensive. bet365’s latest accounts showed pre-tax profit falling from £596 million to £339 million, with the cost of expanding into new overseas markets named as a key reason. Fro Alongside browsing and buying, visitors can enjoy an inspiring programme of talks, live demonstrations and hands-on workshops featuring exciting names from the worlds of craft, design and food. Highlights include free drop-in animation workshops using clay, food and other materia “GNCCF offers a connection you simply can’t get online or on the high street – the chance to meet the makers, hear the stories behind the work and invest in beautifully made pieces that will be cherished for years to come.”

This guided walking tour will bring those stories to life. Led by a local expert, the experience is set to be a lively introduction to the people, places and ideas that have shaped one of the UK’s most influential cities The tour will begin at Manchester Central Library, that impossible to miss, grand circular landmark on St Peter’s Square. The neoclassical design has made it one of the city’s most-loved buildings, holding thousands of stories in its walls and on its shelves. The square itself ha From here, the tour takes you through the city’s heart, down the colourful streets of the Gay Village and the calming Sackville Gardens. It is here that you will see the monuments that honour Manchester’s role in the fight for equality and the city’s pioneering LGBTQ+ community a This guided tour is filled with monuments and tales from many moons ago. The Medieval Quarter is the perfect place to soak in all that history. It is here where you will see the oldest public library in the English-speaking world, Chetham’s Library . Housed in a beautiful sandsto During all this walking, your guide will point out local street art, hidden corners and stories you’d easily miss on your own. Tales of suffragettes, reformers, musicians and everyday Mancunians who’ve all left their mark on the city in their own way

candidates.lead: Bolton Car Boot Sale at Bolton Car Boot Sale
candidates.evidence_text: Bolton Car Boot Sale is one of the North West's biggest weekly boot sales, held in the hardstanding car park of the Macron Stadium (formerly Reebok), Burnden Way, Horwich, Bolton BL6 6JW. It runs every Sunday from February right through to December, drawing over 300 sellers and thousands of bargain hunters each week. Sellers can arrive and set up from 6:00 AM, with buyers welcomed in from 7:00 AM. Entry costs just £1 per car for buyers. Pitches for sellers are £14 for a car, £20 for a van and £3 for a trailer, with regular and corner pitches available on request. Bring exact change to keep the queue moving, and call organiser Andrew on 07470784644 for more details. Expect hundreds of stalls across the concrete hardstanding pitches, so it goes ahead in most weather. On-site you'll find a 5-star catering service, doughnuts and coffee, ice cream and desserts, a meat auction, fresh fruit and veg, plants, and retro sweet stalls. The sale is dog-friendly, has male and female toilets, ample parking, and kids' rides and bouncy castles to keep little ones entertained. After Paul Scholes and Nicky Butt mocked him ahead of Manchester United's clash with Manchester City last season, the defender called the Class of '92 duo out in the mixed zone and contacted them directly to address t In the summer, Martinez and Cristian Romero hit back at Gary Neville after he criticised their defensive partnership for Argentina, at the World Cup. As a member of United's leadership group, even with his track record, it was only right that he stepped up to do the media intervi Martinez admitted he expected more from United in the transfer window . But perhaps the bit that could land him in the most trouble came when he posed the question as to why no-one in the boardroom was facing the pressure of being sacked Get the best United news, updates and analysis straight to your Inbox courtesy of the Manchester Evening News! That comment appeared to be aimed at Jason Wilcox - United's director of football. There are few people more senior than Wilcox and United insist his position is safe . So if that is the case, you would have to presume that consequences are coming for Martinez

candidates.evidence_text: Дронотур Бумбокса Європою. Листопад-грудень 2026 року. Презентація максі-синглу "Живий" Кожного разу, коли перед менеджментом гурту Бумбокс стоїть завдання написати пресреліз, ми починаємо згадувати цікаві факти. Скільки концертів зіграли, скільки грошей зібрали, які пісні видали. Це база. Непогано ще пам’ятати, чи був гурт у країні, до якої ми збираємося, чи це пер О, як би хотілося написати: "Концерт гурту Бумбокс" — і як у Львові за добу продано 8000 квитків. Так-так, ми не про Львів розповідаємо, хоча теж про Європу Наші віддані слухачі, якщо ви перебуваєте за кордоном, сподіваємось, вам буде цікаво дізнатися, що після традиційної перерви на декілька місяців, Бумбокс поїде в турне від Ізраїлю до Німеччини, від Англії до Польщі, від Ірландії до Словаччини та Чехії І повеземо ми в це турне свіженький, як херсонський кавун, максі-сингл “Живий”, підсилений піснями з різних альбомів, під частину яких виросли ви, а під частину зростають ваші діти Тож ознайомтеся, будь ласка, уважно з розкладом туру, купуйте квитки заздалегідь, готуйте гроші на донати та мерч — зустрінемося в листопаді
